title: Granite Switch 4.1.1 — Update models like you update software
gist: IBM shipped Granite Switch 4.1.1, a backwards-compatible patch release that updated only a Granite Speech ASR model and a Decision adapter while leaving the base model untouched. IBM frames its modular adapter architecture as a way to version and ship LLM updates like software, and plans an Adapter SDK for third-party adapter builders.

insights.claim: IBM's Granite Switch 4.1.1 is a patch release that is fully backwards compatible with Granite Switch 4.1, requiring no migration, with version numbers meant to carry software-style semantics.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Semantic versioning for models lowers enterprise upgrade friction and could become a procurement expectation.
insights.quote: The version number means what it means in software: fully backwards compatible with 4.1, no migration, incremental improvements under the hood.
insights.locator: Granite Switch 4.1.1 is a patch release

insights.claim: For Granite Switch 4.1.1, IBM trained only a new ASR model and a new Decision adapter; nothing else was recomputed and the base model was left untouched, so users simply compose the latest adapters and deploy.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Adapter-only updates cut retraining cost and release cadence for enterprise LLM vendors versus full-model refreshes.
insights.quote: Apart from training the new ASR model and Decision adapter, nothing was recomputed: the base model is untouched.
insights.locator: While we are excited about these

insights.claim: IBM shipped Granite Switch 4.1.1 just over a week after Granite Switch 4.1, and says the notable part is the speed and efficiency of the update rather than the features themselves.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Release velocity is becoming a competitive axis for enterprise open models; watch IBM cadence.

insights.claim: IBM is building tutorials and an Adapter SDK so developers and third-party providers can build, version, test and ship their own adapters on the Granite Switch architecture.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: A third-party adapter marketplace would turn Granite into a platform play; watch for SDK launch and partner adapters.
insights.quote: We're working on tutorials and an Adapter SDK so developers and third-party providers can build their own adapters
insights.locator: This pattern can power far more

insights.claim: Granite Switch's modular architecture lets a single endpoint host a language model configured with specialized, cache-efficient adapters, adding new expertise without separate deployments.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Single-endpoint multi-skill serving reduces inference infrastructure sprawl for enterprises.
insights.quote: our modular Switch architecture lets you configure a language model with specialized, cache-efficient adapters — adding new expertise on a single endpoint.

insights.claim: The updated Granite Speech ASR model in Granite Switch 4.1.1 handles multilingual speech-to-text across 10 languages with native punctuation and capitalization, removing a separate formatting pass before downstream models.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Pipeline simplification in speech-to-LLM workflows erodes the value of standalone transcription-cleanup vendors.
insights.quote: multilingual speech-to-text across 10 languages with native punctuation and capitalization, so transcripts are ready for downstream models without a formatting pass.

insights.claim: IBM's updated Decision adapter in granitelib-core improves overall performance on the Jev Decision Index test set, and powers a Speech-to-Decisions demo combining transcription with decisioning.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Shows IBM targeting voice-driven enterprise decision workflows; no numeric gain was disclosed.
